descriptions.job-073sg3r:
Lightspark is creating the Money Grid, modern, open financial infrastructure that makes payments accessible, affordable, and instant for businesses and users worldwide. We're challenging the status quo, updating the current system, and empowering our partners to build better solutions. Together, we're building the most advanced financial infrastructure, open, instant, and global, inspiring a future where anyone, anywhere can access the full potential of digital money.

Lightspark Payments is building regulated services on the Lightning Network and holds Money Transmission Licenses in the United States. This role will lead and manage the licensing and audit function for our regulated payments business, including obtaining and maintaining state licenses, managing regulatory examinations and audits, and driving remediation of any resulting gaps. You will report to our Chief Compliance Officer and will work closely with the Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, Engineering, and Operations teams as Lightspark Payments scales. This role will appeal to experienced licensing and examination professionals who combine rigorous attention to detail with a drive to build better, more scalable processes.

On-site attendance in our Los Angeles office is preferred. We will also consider candidates working remotely, in which case regular travel to our Los Angeles office is required to collaborate with your team and cross functional stakeholders.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Own the end-to-end license lifecycle for Lightspark Payments’ money transmission business: prepare, file, and track new state license applications and change-of-control, key-individual, and other amendment filings in NMLS, and manage renewals and ongoing license maintenance across all states.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for state regulators and, where applicable, federal regulators during licensing cycles, responding to deficiency requests, supplemental information requests, and follow-up inquiries in a timely and complete manner.

  • Maintain a licensing calendar and inventory of license conditions, surety bonds, net worth and permissible investment requirements, registered agents, and renewal deadlines; partner with Finance and Legal to gather the supporting information and documentation.

  • Prepare, review, and submit regulatory reports, including the NMLS MSB Call Report and other periodic state and federal filings, ensuring accuracy, consistency with source data, and on-time submission.

  • Manage regulatory examinations from notification through close-out: coordinate request lists, organize and review document production, prepare management and subject matter experts for interviews, and serve as the day-to-day contact for examiners.

  • Manage the audit program, including bank and partner audits, the annual independent Title 31 BSA/AML audit, and the Compliance Management System (CMS) audit, coordinating with independent auditors and internal stakeholders on scope, timing, evidence, and findings.

  • Lead audit and examination remediation: log findings and gaps, assign owners, define corrective action plans with realistic timelines, track progress to completion, validate that fixes are effective, and report status to the CCO and leadership.

  • Establish and run a quality assurance and monitoring approach for licensing and audit activities, including a central repository of examination responses, audit evidence, and regulatory correspondence that supports consistent and efficient responses over time.

  • Monitor changes in state and federal money transmission laws and regulations (including licensing, surety, reporting, and examination requirements), assess the impact to Lightspark Payments, and work with the CCO and Legal to update policies, procedures, and processes accordingly.

  • Continuously improve licensing and audit processes: identify manual steps and recurring pain points, and design templates, trackers, workflows, and automation that make the function more scalable and audit-ready as Lightspark Payments grows into new states, products, and partners.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Legal to ensure new products, markets, and business changes are evaluated for licensing impact and regulatory notification requirements before launch.

  • Support the CCO and the Compliance Program Manager with the Controls Inventory, risk assessments, policies and procedures, and other compliance program documentation as it relates to licensing and audit findings.

  • Provide direction and work prioritization for the Compliance Analyst supporting licensing and examination activities, and support the CCO as needed.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience working in NMLS, actively applying for and maintaining state money transmission licenses for a licensed money transmitter or similarly regulated fintech.

  • Demonstrated experience interacting directly with state and federal regulators (for example, state banking departments, FinCEN, and the IRS) during both the licensing cycle and examinations, including responding to findings and deficiency requests.

  • Experience preparing and filing the NMLS MSB Call Report and other periodic regulatory reports.

  • Working knowledge of state money transmission laws and the Bank Secrecy Act as applicable to MSBs, and of consumer protection requirements such as Reg E, with familiarity with digital asset or cross-border payments a plus.

  • Proven experience managing examinations and audits (regulatory, bank partner, and independent audits such as Title 31 or CMS) and leading remediation of findings through to closure.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and organization, with the ability to manage many concurrent filings, deadlines, and requests without compromising accuracy.

  • A process-improvement mindset: comfortable building or redesigning processes, trackers, and workflows, and using tools or automation to make licensing and audit work more efficient and repeatable.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the credibility to work with regulators, auditors, executives, and cross-functional teams.

  • Sound judgment and the ability to escalate appropriately to the CCO, balancing regulatory requirements with business needs.

  • Prior experience in a start-up or high-growth environment, or building programs from scratch, is preferred.

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred; relevant certifications (such as CAMS or CRCM) are a plus.

  • Intense professional curiosity and a growth mindset.

Lightspark is on a mission to build the future of open, instant, and global financial infrastructure making payments accessible and affordable for everyone, everywhere. We're committed to creating a more inclusive and diverse workplace to reflect the customers we serve. We welcome interest from individuals of all backgrounds and levels of experience who share our mission. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

 

For US Applicants:

We will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the State of California Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring.

For EU Applicants:

In accordance with applicable EU and local regulations, including the Estonian Employment Contracts Act, Equal Treatment Act, and Gender Equality Act, Lightspark ensures equal treatment throughout the hiring process.

Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.


The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.


We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.


We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.

The Role

You own Banking Experience: the accounts at the center of customer's relationship with the bank, and the API and dashboards they use to manage them.

In this role you’re responsible for redefining what beautiful software in banking looks like. You'll define account structures that give customers powerful building blocks for their products, and craft intuitive interfaces grounded in a deep understanding of their use cases and workflows.

You report to Will, Head of Product, and work closely with Simon, our CTO. You're expected to operate with full autonomy on your team's roadmap, collaborating with design and engineering.

Your First Six Months

  • Months 1-2: Take over day-to-day ownership of the Banking Experience team - the roadmap, the ways of working, the hard decisions. Establish yourself with customers and how they use our accounts. You define and ship your first project.

  • Months 3-4: Execution mode. You're unblocking engineering daily, making hard prioritization calls, and shipping your roadmap to customers. You're proactively raising the bar across accounts, API, and dashboard by feeding what you learn from customers into the product.

  • Months 5-6: You're working with live customers on the products you've built. Deposits and number of account holders are scaling. You've moved from execution to platform mode - evolving the roadmap based on what our customers are building on top of Augustus.

Who Will Thrive At Augustus

We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:

  • American Dream: You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.

  • Live Player: You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.

  • Ever to Excel: You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.

  • Genuine: You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.

This role is for you if:

  • You want to spend time with customers to intimately understand and then innovate on their workflows.

  • You’re a structured and relentless problem solver.

  • You combine first-principles thinking with deep domain knowledge to make complex processes simple.

  • You have taste and care deeply about the quality of what you build.

  • You leverage AI to push the boundaries of what a PM can do.

  • You’re excited about building a programmable bank and helping shape what that means.

Hard Requirements

  • Experience end-to-end owning and building banking, fintech, or developer platform products.

  • Technical enough to spar on architectural decisions with engineers - you're comfortable in API design discussions, not just UI reviews.

  • You have experience with control planes, dashboards, or console products at infrastructure, finance, or developer tools companies.

  • You have strong opinions on information architecture and how to organize complex products so they feel simple

  • Comfortable in customer-facing roles - you've pitched, demoed, and closed early adopters yourself.

  • Based in New York or Berlin, or willing to relocate.

Pay transparency

Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is $180,000-$230,000 + equity.

What We Offer

  • Career Growth: You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.

  • Network: Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.

  • Real Participation: Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.

  • Perks & Benefits: Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.

Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.

Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.

Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission

As an Information Security Specialist, you will own and mature significant parts of our governance, risk, and compliance program in a regulated fintech environment. You’ll be the go-to person for one or more GRC domains (e.g., ISMS and ISO 27001, audit & assurance, third-party risk, risk management, regulatory mapping), driving outcomes end-to-end: control design, operationalization with stakeholders, testing, metrics, and continuous improvement. You’ll operate with high autonomy, influence across teams, and help shape how we scale security governance as the company grows.

What you’ll do 

  • GRC domain ownership & program maturity: Own one or more GRC domains (e.g., ISO 27001/ISMS, control testing, TPRM, risk governance, BCM), including yearly plans, cadence, and measurable outcomes; Build scalable processes and playbooks that reduce audit friction and improve control consistency across teams/entities.
  • Assurance, audits & regulatory readiness: Coordinate internal and external audits end-to-end (readiness planning, walkthroughs, evidence strategy, auditor Q&A, remediation verification); translate new regulatory and customer requirements into control impacts, implementation guidance, and tracked delivery plans; draft and quality-review formal materials: audit responses, management action plans, risk acceptances, and control descriptions.
  • Risk management & decision support: Facilitate and challenge risk assessments for systems, products, and material changes; ensure consistent scoring and clear treatment decisions; drive risk treatment plans with accountable owners; escalate when timelines or residual risk are not acceptable; improve risk reporting for leadership: themes, systemic issues, KRIs/KPIs, and clear prioritization based on business criticality.
  • Third-party risk management (if in your scope): Lead due diligence for critical vendors: define minimum security requirements, review evidence, and track remediation; Partner with Legal/Procurement to embed security requirements into contracts and ensure ongoing oversight (renewals, periodic reviews, SLA/security obligations)
  • Control testing & continuous improvement: Design and run a risk-based control testing plan (design and operating effectiveness), ensuring repeatability and traceability; identify recurring control failures and drive cross-functional improvements (e.g., clearer ownership, automation, better tooling, updated standards); introduce automation and dashboards where useful (e.g., evidence collection, control health reporting, risk and audit tracking).

Who you are 

  • Typically 4-7 years of experience in GRC, audit/assurance, security risk management, compliance, or information security.
  • Strong working knowledge of ISO 27001 (or comparable frameworks) and ability to map requirements to controls, evidence, and real operational processes.
  • Experience leading audits/assessments or significant parts of them (planning through closure).
  • Security fundamentals across IAM, SDLC governance, incident management, vulnerability management, logging/monitoring, and third-party risk concepts.
  • Excellent written communication: can produce policy/control documentation and audit-ready narratives with minimal supervision.

What’s in it for you

  • Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
  • Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
  • Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
  • Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
  • Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
  • Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
  • Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
  • Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
  • Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
  • Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
  • Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

       .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.
* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

What is Kalshi?

Kalshi has defined a new category: prediction markets. Kalshi allows people to trade on the outcome of any events and turn any question about the future into a financial asset. Kalshi fought for years and legalized prediction markets in the US for the first time in history, is currently the fastest growing financial market in America, and has thousands of markets across politics, economics, financials, weather, tech, AI, culture and more.

We believe prediction markets have the potential to be the largest financial market because they turn anything into a financial position.

  • Our vision: well… build the largest financial market on the planet.

  • Our mission: bring more truth to the world through the power of markets.

Our culture is simple: we hire really talented people, work really hard, and enjoy the climb. We are looking for ambitious and exceptional people to join our (relatively small) team to help us build the next generation of financial markets.

Role Roadmap

The core trading experience is where Kalshi’s promise becomes real: understanding a market, placing a trade, and managing a position. Every detail matters, from how an event page explains an outcome to how clearly a trader can see what they own.

We’re looking for a Product Manager to own these experiences across Kalshi’s app, classic web, and Pro platforms. You’ll also own the product experience for non-sports categories, starting with commodities and expanding across finance, politics, and other markets. Your job is to understand what traders in each category need and build experiences that make it easier to start trading and keep coming back.

This is a hands-on role with end-to-end ownership. You’ll set the roadmap, work closely with engineering and design, ship improvements, and measure their impact. Over time, you’ll lead a broader rework of portfolio management, shape how Pro serves more advanced traders, and build a repeatable approach to launching and growing categories.

What You’ll Do

  • Improve event pages, order entry, trading mechanics, and portfolio and position management so customers can understand markets and trade with confidence.

  • Own the category roadmap, starting with commodities. Develop a deep understanding of each audience, improve market pages and category-specific experiences, and partner with markets and growth teams on launches.

  • Spend time with traders, review support feedback, and use product data to identify where customers get confused or drop off. Prioritize the biggest problems and follow through from discovery to launch.

  • Close gaps across the app, classic web, and Pro. Decide which experiences should be consistent and where advanced traders need different capabilities.

  • Help traders understand their positions, track performance, and take action through clear, intuitive product experiences.

  • Develop and test experiences such as alerts, watchlists, and recurring markets that support ongoing engagement within non-sports categories.

  • Define category and product metrics, build dashboards with analytics partners, and run experiments to understand what improves trading conversion, engagement, and retention.

  • Work closely with engineering, design, markets and operations, support, and compliance. Make clear decisions, resolve tradeoffs, and stay involved in the details through QA and release.

What You Bring

  • You’ve shipped customer-facing products and understand what makes a consumer app intuitive, useful, and worth returning to.

  • You can spot confusing interactions, simplify complex workflows, and partner with designers to turn a good idea into a great experience.

  • You can take an ambiguous problem, define what matters, set priorities, and personally drive the work through launch and iteration.

  • You understand how traders think about markets and positions, ideally with familiarity across commodities and macro, and can speak credibly about what these customers need.

  • You’re comfortable using data, customer research, and experiments to diagnose problems, make decisions, and measure whether a change worked.

  • You move quickly, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and care about the small details that determine whether a product works well.

  • You can align teams around a problem, explain your decisions, and work through technical, operational, and compliance constraints.

Bonus

  • Experience building trading, investing, prediction market, or consumer financial products.

  • Firsthand use of trading or sports betting products, with a clear point of view on what makes their customer experiences work.

  • Experience owning products across mobile and web, building tools for advanced users, or launching and growing new product categories.

NYC Pay Transparency Disclosure

Salary Range: $150,000-$250,000 annually plus equity and benefits. This salary range is based on the current available market data, and represents the expected salary range for this role. Kalshi has minimal hierarchy and few titles, but has broad ranges of experience represented within roles. Should you have compensation expectations that exceed these bands, we'd love to hear from you and would welcome you to reach out to further discuss.

Our Culture

Meritocracy is at our core, and we value people who take ownership and figure (usually hard) things out. We dream big. We love our craft deeply and are proud of what we put out in the world. We are committed to our vision of building something big… but also useful: a product that brings more truth through the power of markets.

Kalshians are Kalshi’s most important asset: we pick Kalshians carefully, so we trust them fully on day 1.

We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

About the team

The APAC Payments TechOps team ensures the accuracy of financial data flowing through Stripe's payment infrastructure, manages aging balances, maintains compliance with partner and regulatory requirements, and builds tooling to detect and resolve data quality issues at scale. Through the internship, you will work with real financial data, gain experience in payments data analysis and operational problem-solving, and have opportunities to present your work to your team and the wider org. Each intern has a dedicated intern manager, and every project is part of the team's roadmap and will directly help Stripe's mission.

What you’ll do

Every internship at Stripe centers around a real, legitimate project that our team urgently needs. We will support you in shipping it. Yes, you will actually ship it. Example projects include building data quality checks for payment flows, creating dashboards to surface aging balance trends, automating compliance reporting, or analyzing cost structures across partner networks. As a Stripe intern, you'll be tackling important projects while working alongside exceptional people who insist on doing their best work. You'll learn from people with high standards who are great at inspiring others to do more and go further. We value technical and personal growth, and see our internship program as a vehicle to foster both.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze financial data by writing queries and examining data quality, reconciliation accuracy, or cost structures across Stripe's payment flows
  • Write code or build tooling that will be used in production and has meaningful impact to Stripe's payment operations
  • Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews, data model discussions, or analysis walkthroughs
  • Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and finance stakeholders to seek and incorporate feedback on your work
  • Learn quickly by asking great questions, by working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, and by communicating the status of your work clearly

Who you are

  • Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
  • Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.

Minimum requirements

  • A strong fundamental understanding of quantitative analysis through pursuit of a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in computer science, data science, finance, economics, information systems, or a related discipline
  • Some experience and familiarity with programming or data analysis, either through side projects or coursework. We work mostly in SQL, Python, and Ruby. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
  • Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders
  • Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

Preferred qualifications

  • Familiarity with SQL and querying relational databases, either through coursework or personal projects
  • Interest in payments, fintech, or financial systems
  • Comfort with developer tools (e.g. git) and data visualization
  • A strong interest in understanding how financial data flows through complex payment systems and ensuring its accuracy

Interviewing with TRM

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

About Matter Labs

Matter Labs builds private cryptographic infrastructure that lets regulated institutions settle directly with each other without exposing data, ceding control, or waiting days. Global finance moves $4 quadrillion a year on systems designed for paper and telex. The institutions that built them - from clearing houses to exchanges to the world's largest banks, institutions are now actively replacing them. We're building what comes next.

Our core product, Prividium, gives each institution its own private environment (a Prividium Zone) with independent governance and built-in interoperability across counterparties, asset classes, and jurisdictions. Interoperability happens through zero-knowledge proofs: one party proves a transaction is valid without revealing any underlying data to the counterparty. The only private settlement infrastructure built on zero-knowledge cryptography.

Founded in 2018. Backed by a16z and Union Square Ventures. A fully remote team of around 70 with eight years of production zero-knowledge infrastructure behind us, now pointed at the biggest problem in institutional finance.

The role

You will be the engineer embedded with our institutional customers, taking Prividium from a signed deal to a live chain inside their environment. The institutions running on it are banks, custodians, and clearing houses moving real value on infrastructure built decades ago. What you deploy becomes part of how they operate.

Requirements from an institution arrive as a description of the system being replaced, because that is how large organizations specify work, and because the obligations underneath are decades of accumulated regulation, audit, and control. Reading through to those obligations is the hard part of this job. We need someone who can find them, design the general thing that satisfies them for this customer and the next four, and put it in front of the customer's engineers as a firm recommendation they can push back on.

What you will do:

  • Own deployments end to end: integration code, permissioning, node topology, upgrade paths, and the runbook the customer's ops team will use.

  • Build the reference applications that prove a use case, across collateral movement, tokenized deposit transfer, and settlement flows.

  • Carry the pager for Prividium and the services we run around it, including the night something breaks and the fix that stops it breaking again.

  • Work with the Head of Product and Head of Sales on which accounts to go deep on, and with our core engineering team on what graduates from a deployment into the platform.

The people who do well here would rather ship a rough working version on Thursday than present a diagram on Friday. They can say how confident they are in a recommendation and what would change their mind. The rarest trait is taste: seeing the good general solution inside a hard set of constraints and telling it apart from the merely clever one.

Requirements

  • Production software you have owned and run, including carrying a pager for it.

  • A strong coder. TypeScript or Rust in your day to day, or deep fluency in a comparable language such as Java, C#, Go, or Python and the ability to pick ours up fast.

  • Serious time inside customer environments, whether as a forward deployed engineer, a solutions architect, or a technical founder. Former founders are strongly encouraged to apply.

We are hiring two people into this role and we are not looking for one person who covers both of the areas below. Depth in one is what matters.

If you come from banking

  • Experience building or integrating software for financial institutions or regulated financial infrastructure.

  • Working knowledge of the systems banks run: core banking platforms, custody and key management, identity and entitlements, ISO 20022 or comparable messaging standards, enterprise auth and network architecture.

  • Fluency with risk, compliance, controls, SLAs, and procurement.

  • No blockchain experience required. We will teach you the stack.

If you come from crypto infrastructure

  • Experience with Ethereum execution clients and node internals. Direct reth experience is a strong signal.

  • Rust in production, since that is where the node work lives.

  • Comfortable operating chain infrastructure in production: node topology, upgrades, sync and reorg behavior, monitoring.

  • Experience with Solidity or readiness to learn it quickly and a working understanding of rollup and bridging mechanics.

  • Able to explain cryptographic trust guarantees to audiences who do not have that background.

Work model & pay

  • Competitive base salary

  • Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional. Both are paid in ZK tokens. New-hire token grants vest over four years with a one-year cliff.

  • Fully remote, with roughly 10 to 25 percent travel to customer sites depending on which accounts you carry.

  • Shared on-call rotation covering Prividium and our hosted services. Everyone in this role is on it.

  • Our customers are in North America and Europe, so we need working-hours overlap with those time zones.
